options.A: dealer sells two tractor models, X and Y, at the same cost price (CP). Model X is sold at a profit of 15%, while Model Y is sold at a loss of 10%. If the total profit earned from selling one unit of each model is Rs 6,000, what is the cost price of each model?

questions.solution:
Q.1 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Quantitative Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 1Q.1  |  General Aptitude  |  Quantitative AptitudeType: MCQ   |   Marks: 1Question:A dealer sells two tractor models, X and Y, at the same cost price (CP). Model X is sold at a profit of 15%, while Model Y is sold at a loss of 10%. If the total profit earned from selling one unit of each model is Rs 6,000, what is the cost price of each model?(A) Rs 1,00,000(B) Rs 1,10,000(C) Rs 1,20,000(D) Rs 1,30,000Answer: CExplanation:Net gain per pair of transactions = 15% of CP − 10% of CP = 5% of CP. This equals Rs 6,000, so CP = 6000/0.05 = Rs 1,20,000.Why others are wrong: (A) and (B) result from mistakenly using the difference 15%−10%=5% but dividing 6000 by a wrong base (e.g. treating 6000 as 6% or applying it to only one transaction). (D) results from adding instead of subtracting the percentages (25% base), giving an inflated CP.

questions.question: [MCQ] Two identical seed drills, A and B, working together can sow a field in 6 hours. Working alone, Drill A takes 5 hours less than Drill B. How long does Drill A alone take to sow the field?

options.A: 8 hours

questions.solution:
Q.2 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Quantitative Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 1Q.2  |  General Aptitude  |  Quantitative AptitudeType: MCQ   |   Marks: 1Question:Two identical seed drills, A and B, working together can sow a field in 6 hours. Working alone, Drill A takes 5 hours less than Drill B. How long does Drill A alone take to sow the field?(A) 8 hours(B) 9 hours(C) 10 hours(D) 12 hoursAnswer: CExplanation:Let A take t hours alone, so B takes (t+5) hours. Combined rate: 1/t + 1/(t+5) = 1/6. Multiplying: 6(t+5) + 6t = t(t+5) → 12t + 30 = t² + 5t → t² − 7t − 30 = 0 → (t−10)(t+3) = 0 → t = 10 (rejecting the negative root).Why others are wrong: (A) 8 and (B) 9 do not satisfy the quadratic exactly (a quick check: 1/8+1/13 ≠ 1/6; 1/9+1/14 ≠ 1/6). (D) 12 is the value one gets by incorrectly assuming B alone takes 2×6=12 h and reasoning informally, which does not satisfy the combined-rate equation.

questions.question: [MCQ] Five farm engineers — P, Q, R, S, T — sit in a row of five chairs facing north, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. R sits third to the left of T. Q sits immediately to the right of R. S sits at one of the two end seats and is not adjacent to Q. P sits between Q and T.Who sits at the leftmost end (seat 1)?

options.A: P

questions.solution:
Q.4 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Analytical Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 1Q.4  |  General Aptitude  |  Analytical AptitudeType: MCQ   |   Marks: 1Question:Five farm engineers — P, Q, R, S, T — sit in a row of five chairs facing north, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. R sits third to the left of T. Q sits immediately to the right of R. S sits at one of the two end seats and is not adjacent to Q. P sits between Q and T.Who sits at the leftmost end (seat 1)?(A) P(B) Q(C) R(D) SAnswer: CExplanation:"R third to the left of T" means position(T) = position(R) + 3. Taking R = 1 gives T = 4. Since Q is immediately right of R, Q = 2. P sits between Q(2) and T(4), so P = 3. The only remaining seat is 5, which must be S — and seat 5 is indeed an end seat and not adjacent to Q(2), satisfying all conditions. The final order is R, Q, P, T, S, so seat 1 is R.Why others are wrong: (A) P occupies seat 3, the middle, not the end. (B) Q occupies seat 2. (D) S occupies seat 5, the right end, not the left end.

It returns from B to A by the same route at a uniform speed, and the total round-trip time is 7 hours. What is the return speed?

questions.solution:

options.A: 18 years

What is the supervisor's present age?(A) 18 years(B) 21 years(C) 24 years(D) 27 yearsAnswer: CExplanation:Let the trainee's present age be x, so the supervisor's is 3x. questions.question: [MCQ] Consider the statement: "All combine harvesters manufactured after 2020 at the plant have GPS auto-steer. Machine Z has GPS auto-steer."Which one of the following can be logically concluded from this statement alone?

options.A: Machine Z was manufactured after 2020 at the plant.
options.B: Machine Z was manufactured at the plant, but the year cannot be determined from the statement.
options.C: No valid conclusion regarding the manufacturing year or location of Machine Z can be drawn from the statement.
options.D: Machine Z was definitely not manufactured before 2020.

questions.solution:
Q.8 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Verbal Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 2Q.8  |  General Aptitude  |  Verbal AptitudeType: MCQ   |   Marks: 2Question:Consider the statement: "All combine harvesters manufactured after 2020 at the plant have GPS auto-steer. Machine Z has GPS auto-steer."Which one of the following can be logically concluded from this statement alone?(A) Machine Z was manufactured after 2020 at the plant.(B) Machine Z was manufactured at the plant, but the year cannot be determined from the statement.(C) No valid conclusion regarding the manufacturing year or location of Machine Z can be drawn from the statement.(D) Machine Z was definitely not manufactured before 2020.Answer: CExplanation:The statement is a one-directional conditional: (manufactured after 2020 at the plant) → (has GPS auto-steer). Knowing that Z has GPS auto-steer does not allow us to infer the reverse (that Z was made after 2020 at that plant) — Z could have GPS auto-steer for an entirely different reason (another manufacturer, a retrofit, etc.). Concluding otherwise commits the logical fallacy of affirming the consequent, so no valid conclusion about Z's year or place of manufacture can be drawn.Why others are wrong: (A), (B) and (D) all attempt to infer something about Z's manufacturing year or location from the fact that it has GPS auto-steer, which is exactly the invalid inference (affirming the consequent) that the statement does not support.

options.A: The rated engine power

questions.question: [MCQ] The specific yield of an unconfined aquifer represents:

options.A: The total porosity of the aquifer material
options.B: The volume of water released per unit surface area per unit decline in the water table, expressed as a fraction of the total volume
options.C: The hydraulic conductivity of the aquifer
options.D: The storage coefficient of a confined aquifer

questions.solution:
Q.27 Solution:• Correct Answer: B• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Groundwater Hydrology | Type: MCQ | Marks: 1Q.27  |  S5 — Irrigation & Drainage Engineering  |  Groundwater HydrologyType: MCQ   |   Marks: 1Question:The specific yield of an unconfined aquifer represents:(A) The total porosity of the aquifer material(B) The volume of water released per unit surface area per unit decline in the water table, expressed as a fraction of the total volume(C) The hydraulic conductivity of the aquifer(D) The storage coefficient of a confined aquiferAnswer: BExplanation:Specific yield is defined as the volume of water that drains freely from a unit volume of saturated aquifer material under gravity per unit decline in water table (i.e., the "drainable porosity"), expressed as a fraction of the total aquifer volume.Why others are wrong: (A) Total porosity includes both drainable (specific yield) and retained (specific retention) water and is therefore larger than specific yield. options.C: The relative humidity of the ambient air only

questions.question: [MSQ — one or more correct] Which of the following statement(s) regarding size-reduction equipment and theory is/are CORRECT?

questions.question: [MSQ — one or more correct] Which of the following statement(s) regarding heat transfer in food-processing equipment is/are CORRECT?

options.A: In steady-state conduction through a composite slab (layers in series), the overall thermal resistance equals the sum of the individual layer resistances.
options.B: The overall heat transfer coefficient U in a heat exchanger is always numerically greater than the highest individual film heat transfer coefficient.
options.C: Fouling on heat-exchanger surfaces increases thermal resistance and decreases the overall heat transfer coefficient U.
options.D: In natural (free) convection, fluid motion is induced by density differences arising from temperature gradients.

questions.solution:
Q.63 Solution:• Correct Answer: A, C, D• Section: Agricultural Engineering | Sub-topic: Heat and Mass Transfer | Type: MSQ | Marks: 2Q.63  |  S7 — Dairy & Food Engineering  |  Heat and Mass TransferType: MSQ   |   Marks: 2Question:Which of the following statement(s) regarding heat transfer in food-processing equipment is/are CORRECT?(A) In steady-state conduction through a composite slab (layers in series), the overall thermal resistance equals the sum of the individual layer resistances.(B) The overall heat transfer coefficient U in a heat exchanger is always numerically greater than the highest individual film heat transfer coefficient.(C) Fouling on heat-exchanger surfaces increases thermal resistance and decreases the overall heat transfer coefficient U.(D) In natural (free) convection, fluid motion is induced by density differences arising from temperature gradients.Answer: A, C, DExplanation:(A) Correct — for series (layered) conduction resistances, 1/U (or total R) equals the sum of the individual layer resistances, exactly analogous to resistances in series in an electrical circuit. (D) Correct — natural convection is driven precisely by buoyancy-induced density differences resulting from temperature gradients within the fluid.(B) is incorrect — because resistances add in series, the overall coefficient U is always less than (never greater than) the smallest individual film coefficient in the series, not greater than the largest one.

questions.question: [MSQ — one or more correct] Which of the following statement(s) regarding food preservation techniques is/are CORRECT?

options.A: Osmotic dehydration primarily removes water by immersing food in a hypertonic solution, relying on the osmotic pressure difference across the food's cell membranes.
options.B: Freeze-drying (lyophilization) removes water via sublimation of ice under vacuum, and generally yields better retention of quality attributes than hot-air drying.
options.C: Blanching prior to freezing is done mainly to inactivate enzymes that would otherwise cause quality deterioration during frozen storage.
options.D: Food irradiation substantially raises the bulk temperature of the food, and preservation is achieved primarily through this thermal effect.

(C) Correct — blanching's primary purpose before freezing is enzyme inactivation (e.g. polyphenol oxidase, peroxidase) to prevent off-flavours, discoloration and nutrient loss during frozen storage.(D) is incorrect — irradiation is fundamentally a non-thermal (or only minimally thermal) preservation process; it works through ionizing radiation damaging microbial and enzymatic DNA/cellular structures, not through bulk heating of the food.
